 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 deceased Sri.Kumara @ Kumar S/o late Krishnappa, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 02.06.2023 at 07.50 p.m, the deceased Kumara @ Kumar was proceeding by walk on the extreme left side of the footpath road from NH-75, Bengaluru - Mangaluru Highway, at the same time the driver of Car bearing No.KA-01-MH-6979 came from Bengaluru, NH-75 Road side, in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed against deceased Kumara @ Kumar.

Due to which the deceased Kumara @
Kumar sustained severe head injury and other injury all over the body and immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, Nagamangala, but inspite of better treatment given by the doctors at the said hospital, he succumbed to the injuries at about 11.20 p.m.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses etc., funeral and obsequies.
Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged 39 years and was doing Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioner No.3 is the mother of
the (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 deceased were solely depending on the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioner's lost the main earning member of their family and also lost love and affection and suffering from severe shock.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of above said Car by its driver and in this regard the Bellur Police have registered a case against driver of the said Car.
The respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Car
, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, he was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and denies issuance of policy bearing No.1415223231 10013067 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Car bearing No.KA-01-MH-6979 and its validity since it is not confirmed by the concerned policy issuing office and the liability of this respondent, if any, is strictly in terms and conditions,
Lakshmi vs Lohith Gowda K.P on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119643233/
2 exceptions, limits and (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 endorsement of the policy and further denied age, occupation, income of deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and dependency of the petitioners and manner of accident and involvement of the offending Car in the accident.

The respondent No.1 had been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident, thereby, there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Sec.150(2) of M.V. Act, hence,
this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation and the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.

Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against the respondent No.2.
05.
On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Kumara S/o late Krishnappa?

02. Whether petitioner prove that deceased Sri.Kumara S/o late Krishnappa was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 02.06.2023 at about 7.50 p.m, Halalu Gate, Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75 Road, (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-01-MH-6979 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04. What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 and closed their side evidence.

On the otherhand, the respondent No.2 counsel submits no oral evidence, hence, the respondent No.2 evidence is taken as nil and closed respondents side evidence.
07.
Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Despite sufficient opportunity, the petitioners have not advanced their arguments, hence, petitioners side arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 Lakshmi vs Lohith Gowda K.P on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119643233/
3  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 09. Issue No.1 & 2:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
10.
The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.
Though, she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is elicited from her mouth to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 14 documents as Ex.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Bellur Police against driver of offending Car for his rash and negligent driving and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged against driver of offending Car.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Seizer Mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Inquest Panchanama of deceased Kumara @ Kumar.

Ex.P.6 is copy of Post mortem report of (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 deceased Kumara @ Kumar which shows the cause of death is due to cranio cerebral injuries as a result of blunt force impact to head.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending Car and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and caused accident and caused death of deceased.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Aadhaar card of deceased Kumara @ Kumar.
Ex.P.9 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1.
Ex.P.10 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.2.
Ex.P.11 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.3 and Ex.P.12 is copy of IMV report which indicates involvement of the offending car in the alleged accident.

12. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence, the petitioners have proved and established that the deceased Kumara @ Kumar was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 02.06.2023 at 07.50 p.m, near Halalu Gate, Bengaluru-Mangalore NH-75 Road, Bellur Hobli,
Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya, due to negligent act of driving of Car bearing No.KA-01-MH-6979, by its driver.

It is also further proved as per Ex.P.8 to 11 Aadhaar cards of the petitioners that the petitioner (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioner No.3 is the mother of deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.
Accordingly, these Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Kumara @ Kumar, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

PW.1/petitioner No.1 who is the wife of the deceased has stated that as on the date of alleged accident the the deceased was aged about 39 years and was doing Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and due to death of the deceased, they are put to severe shock and lost love and affection and they have spent Rs.1,00,000/-
Lakshmi vs Lohith Gowda K.P on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119643233/
4 towards medical expenses etc., funeral and obsequies.
14.
It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any school records, SSLC marks card or birth certificate of the deceased to show the date of birth of the deceased.
But they have produced Ex.P.8 copy of Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, even in the absence of cogent evidence with (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 respect to date of birth of deceased, the said document can be relied upon.
According to which the deceased date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1983 and the alleged accident occurred on 02.06.2023.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of deceased is 40 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 40 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 36 to 40 years is 15.
15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though the petitioners have claimed that the deceased was working as Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m, but the petitioners have not produced any documents or evidence for the proof of avocation and income of the deceased.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory evidence regarding the avocation and income of the deceased, this tribunal has relied upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru, the notional income as per the year 2023 is Rs.16,000/-.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.

(SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 16. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects of the deceased is taking into consideration.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was aged 40 years at the time of the accident, 40% of the income is required to be added to the monthly income towards future prospectus, which would result in the income to be (16,000 + 6,400) Rs.22,400/-.

There are 3 dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (22,400 - 7,467) Rs.14,933/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.14,933/-.
As the deceased was aged 40 years, a multiplier of 15 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.26,87,940/- (Rs.14,933 x 12 x 15) towards loss of dependency.

17. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 10% in every 3 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
18. Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.13 Medical bills, the petitioners have incurred medical expenses of Rs.16,459/- for the treatment of deceased Kumara @ Kumar.

Therefore, the petitioners are Lakshmi vs Lohith Gowda K.P on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119643233/
5 entitled for Rs.16,459/- under this head.
19.
The claimant No.1 the wife, claimant No.2 the minor daughter and claimant No.3 the mother of deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium.
Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of parental consortium and petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/3rd of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased and medical expenses, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
 (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4829/2023  Sl. Head of Compensation Amount in  No. Rs.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 . Loss of Dependency 26,87,940-00  (After deducting 1/3rd of the  income towards personal and  living expenses)

2. Medical expenses 16,459-00  3. Loss of spousal consortium 48,000-00  (for petitioner No.1)
 4. Loss of parental consortium 48,000-00  (for petitioner No.2)
 5. Loss of filial consortium (for 48,000-00  petitioner No.3)
 6. Loss of estate 18,000-00
7 . Funeral expenses and 18,000-00  transportation of dead body  Total 28,84,399-00 20.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,84,399/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

21. Regarding liability:- Though the respondent No.2 has taken several defences in its written statement, but even despite sufficient opportunity has been given to the respondent No.2, but has not lead any evidence to disprove the case of (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 the petitioners.
Therefore, as per the averments made in the petition, the insurance policy of the offending car is valid from 28.02.2023 to 27.02.2024.
The alleged accident occurred on 02.06.2023.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force.

Further, the respondent No.1 was remained absent and was placed exparte and there is no evidence on record to show that the driver or the owner of the offending vehicle have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Hence, respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since insurance policy of the offending Lakshmi vs Lohith Gowda K.P on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119643233/
6 vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer shall liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.28,84,399/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a within two months from the date of this Judgment.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
 (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.4829/2023  ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.28,84,399/- (Rupees Twenty eight lakhs eighty four thousand three hundred and ninety nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 being the minor daughter and petitioner No.3 being the mother of deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 60-20-20, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 3 are entitled to get release 70% each in the award amount through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.4829/2023 Since the petitioner No.2 is minor, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioner No.2 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attains the age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest periodically in the name of minor petitioner No.2 by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.2.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
